doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Audio interlude and the Red Tyler album on Rounder
summary: After hearing a clip, he recalls the Rounder recording with Red Tyler, fifteen or sixteen takes of one tune, and accepting his imperfect take.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah. I have a little piece of music for you to listen to.
Yeah. That brings back memories man.
That’s a great moment there. I mean everybody’s in the moment and they’re listening to you and reacting to you.
Yeah, it’s funny man, about that particular, that was the title of the album, I forgot the name of the album, it was with Red Tyler.

On the Rounder label. Red Tyler was one of those musicians that was in my living room in the forties. And this particular tune, the guy was from Boston with the Rounder label. And when we first started playing that tune man, my chops was good, I was playing high, I was playing all this, but I didn’t know what the producer was looking for so we did about fifteen, sixteen takes, one day, of that particular tune. And then when we came back we did almost that same amount that day. So to me when you keep repeating it, instead of going up, it goes down, a lack of interest and energy. So that particular take, man, it was one of those that, I mean it’s okay the way I play and all but I wish he would have taken the first couple of ones, but it wasn’t on the record. So the saxophone player, he had picked the one that he liked best. But jazz music wasn’t created under the ideal situations. It came out of a lot of diversity and stuff like that. So with all the mistakes — even I remember there was a critic in Boston when they first heard that, they said yeah the trumpet player missed a note or something like that, but he didn’t know how many times I played that song and my lips were getting tired. You know you play a brass instrument, man. So but I still love it because it shows my human quality. I’m not perfect you know.
